main.title: Little Lantern Friends
main.goal: Build shared games that help Mina and Emre learn how to include each other.
main.stakes: Small misunderstandings can make a new friendship harder, while patient play can build trust.
main.central_mystery: What kinds of play help each child feel brave enough to join?

approved_premise.title: The Lantern That Moved
approved_premise.logline: When a gust moves one lantern from the pretend trail, Mina can turn the small problem into a way for shy Emre to help shape the game.
approved_premise.protagonist_role: Mina is an active four-year-old play leader, not a passive observer.
approved_premise.immediate_objective: Put the lantern trail back together in a way that gives Emre a comfortable part to play.
approved_premise.inciting_event: A gust rolls one paper lantern away from its chalk mark just as the game is about to begin.
approved_premise.central_problem: Mina wants to fix the trail quickly, but the better solution may require listening to Emre's idea.
approved_premise.wonder_or_discovery: The moved lantern can become a new pretend destination rather than merely a mistake.
approved_premise.stakes: If Mina rushes, Emre may stay on the edge of the game; if she includes him, they can make something new together.
constraints: Keep all tension mild and safe.
Adults may supervise but must not solve the play problem.
Pretend magic must remain clearly imaginative.
approved_premise.meaningful_choice_pressure: No strategic branch is required; Mina should still make a visible participatory choice about how to include Emre.
approved_premise.mystery_or_forward_question: What new pretend place will they invent together next?
approved_premise.local_payoff: Resolve the small lantern problem and give both children an active shared moment.
persistent_outcomes_possible: Mina and Emre may gain a small friendship memory if both participate.

creation_constraints: New play details must stay transient and imaginative.
forbidden_creations: Adult solving the central play problem
